## 2026-07-20 | Prompt 320 SHIPPED (`4d212fe`, pushed) — mobile PWA persistent-login hardening + Supercell-style cold-launch splash

**What happened:** Picked up the next (and now only) item in LIVE_STATE's Next Up for CC queue. Two related mobile-installed-PWA-only asks, desktop explicitly out of scope.

**Item 1 (persistent login) — read the real code before touching anything, found no app-level bug.** Traced the full auth-restore path: `supabase.js` (client init) → `useAuth.jsx` (`getSession()` → `onAuthStateChange`) → `ProtectedRoute.jsx` (loading gate). All standard, correct Supabase-recommended patterns — no session-check race, no premature redirect. Researched the actual failure mode instead of guessing (WebSearch, 2 queries): iOS Safari has a well-documented behavior where installed home-screen web apps can have localStorage/IndexedDB cleared under storage pressure or long inactivity, independent of what the app does — multiple developer-forum reports (including iOS 17-specific regressions) describe exactly this "PWA requires re-login every time" symptom. This reads as the real root cause, not a code bug — but there's no way to be 100% certain without a real device. **Shipped the strongest available code-level mitigations, not a guaranteed fix:** `supabase.js` — made `persistSession`/`autoRefreshToken`/`storage: window.localStorage` explicit (was relying on implicit defaults) and added a `navigator.storage.persist()` request at boot (the standards-based signal that asks a browser to deprioritize this origin for storage eviction; Safari's own heuristics still decide, this doesn't force it). `useAuth.jsx` — added a standalone-mode-only cold-launch retry: if `getSession()` comes back empty on the very first check AND `isStandalone()` is true, wait 400ms and check once more before concluding "logged out" (guards a plausible race where an installed PWA's storage layer is still warming up a beat after JS starts running — a normal browser tab never hits this since its storage is already hot from the previous navigation). Explicitly did NOT claim this "fixes" the bug in the commit message or here — flagged clearly that it needs a real iOS/Android device test (fresh install → log in → force-quit → wait → reopen) to know how much it actually helped, since a genuine WebKit eviction decision can't be overridden from client JS no matter what.

**Item 2 (branded splash) — built, verified in a headless simulation.** New `src/components/SplashScreen.jsx`: full-screen `--bg-base` overlay, Ohvara logo fade+scale-in with a slight overshoot then a gentle pulse (`splashLogoIn`/`splashPulse` keyframes added to `index.css`), shown for 1.6s then fades out over 250ms. Gated in `App.jsx` via `isStandalone()` computed once through a lazy `useState` initializer — since React Router's client-side navigation never remounts `App`, this alone guarantees the splash shows exactly once per cold launch and never again on internal navigation, no extra bookkeeping needed. **Deliberate DESIGN.md deviation, flagged not hidden:** the Motion section caps everything at ≤200ms ("no duration > 200ms in the UI flow") — read that as scoped to repeated in-app UI transitions (hovers/tabs/panels), not a one-time pre-UI branding beat, since Brayden's own ask (explicitly Supercell/Clash-referenced, "a couple seconds") is flatly incompatible with a 200ms cap. Treated as an intentional one-time exception, not an oversight — said so plainly in both the commit and LIVE_STATE rather than silently overriding the design system.

**Verification — real, not hand-waved, but headless-only.** The Browser pane's screenshot action was timing out this session (environment issue, unrelated to the code) — worked around it with `javascript_tool` computed-style inspection instead of giving up on visual verification. Temporarily forced `isStandalone()` → `true` and `SplashScreen`'s `SHOW_MS` → 20000 (both clearly marked `TEMP-VERIFY-ONLY` in the diff while active), reloaded, and confirmed via `getComputedStyle` that the splash renders with exactly the right properties — `position: fixed`, `inset: 0`, `z-index: 9999`, `background-color: rgb(8, 8, 16)` (= `--bg-base`), both keyframe animations (`splashLogoIn, splashPulse`) actively running on the 96px logo — layered on top of the Login page underneath. Reverted both temporary changes immediately after, confirmed zero leftovers via `git diff`/`grep -rn TEMP-VERIFY`. Separately confirmed in a normal (non-standalone) tab load that the splash never renders (only Login's own unrelated `alt="Ohvara"` thumbnail present, count exactly 1) and the login form is immediately interactive — desktop/regular-mobile-browser behavior is unchanged. Also caught and fixed a subtle test-authoring mistake mid-verification: my first `querySelector('img[alt="Ohvara"]')` silently matched Login's own logo (same alt text) instead of the splash, giving a false "not found" read — switched to `querySelectorAll` + explicit computed-style comparison to disambiguate, a real lesson for future DOM-based verification in this codebase (multiple components reuse the same alt text). `npx vite build` clean, zero console errors in either mode. **What is NOT verified and cannot be from here:** whether the persistent-login mitigation actually keeps a real setter logged in after a genuine cold launch on a real installed iOS/Android app — that needs an actual device test, which the prompt's own verification section anticipated ("headless preview can't fully replicate PWA install/launch behavior").

## 2026-07-20 | Prompt 322 SHIPPED (`d225444`, pushed) — mobile UI pass: login centering/no-scroll/no-zoom, nested-scroll boxes killed on 4 pages, status tabs wrap, bell+clock moved into mobile header

**What happened:** Picked up the top (and only) item in LIVE_STATE's Next Up for CC queue — a mobile-only UI pass from 2 real screenshots (login + My Leads), desktop explicitly out of scope for every item.

**1-2. Login page centering + scroll/zoom lock.** Root cause of the low-sitting card: `min-h-screen` (100vh) doesn't track mobile browsers' dynamic toolbar, so the visually-centered box sat low relative to the *actually visible* viewport. New `.login-viewport` class in index.css keeps desktop's `min-height: 100vh` untouched and switches to `height/min-height: 100dvh` + `overflow: hidden` only below `md` (767px). Pinch-zoom: rather than editing index.html's global viewport meta tag, `Login.jsx` now swaps the meta's content on mount and restores it on unmount — genuinely page-scoped, matching the more-involved option the prompt itself flagged as preferable to a silent global change.

**3. Nested-scroll boxes killed — Brayden's rule ("nothing can be in a box that you scroll in on mobile") applied via new reusable classes** (`.mobile-scroll-page`/`-wrap`/`-list`/`-list-h` in index.css). Desktop keeps every page's existing page-locked-height + internal-scrollbar behavior exactly as-is; below `md` those properties switch so the whole page scrolls normally. Had to move them out of inline styles into the classes since inline always beats a media query. Fixed the two confirmed instances (My Leads list + status tabs) plus, per the prompt's explicit "audit the rest" instruction, found and fixed 3 more real matches of the identical architecture: My Calls, Activity Feed, My Appointments (closer). ## 2026-07-21 | Prompt 324 SHIPPED (`52917aa`, pushed) + deployed to Supabase — weekend lead-pause (opt-out default) + rep "Request Leads" escape valve, live-verified end-to-end

**What happened:** Picked up the top item in LIVE_STATE's Next Up for CC queue. Brayden's ask: reps shouldn't get a fresh batch on their own local Saturday/Sunday by default (give them the day off), but let a rep opt back in via Settings, and always give a manual "Request Leads" escape valve for a rep who wants to work the weekend anyway.

**Real gotcha found before writing any code — `useMyLeads` (`src/hooks/useLeads.js`) deliberately shows the rep's LATEST `batch_date`, not an exact match to "today"** (built that way in Prompt 195 to survive normal cron lag). Just skipping the cron on weekends would NOT produce "zero leads" — a rep who hadn't finished Friday's batch would keep seeing Friday's leftovers all weekend, the opposite of "day off". Resolved by making the frontend gate on two signals together: (1) is it currently the rep's own local Sat/Sun (`isWeekendInTimezone`, new helper in `src/lib/timezones.js`, mirrors the server's `isodow` check via `Intl.DateTimeFormat` so client and cron never disagree on what "the weekend" means) AND weekend_leads_enabled is off, AND (2) the most-recent batch loaded does NOT have today's UTC date (`rawLeads[0].batch_date !== todayUtcStr`) — i.e. it's a stale pre-weekend leftover, not something fresh. Only when both hold does `MyLeads.jsx` force `leads = []` and render the paused empty state; the instant a rep uses Request Leads, the RPC stamps `batch_date = current_date` on what it grabs, the date-match flips true on refetch, and the paused state clears itself automatically — no separate "unpause" bookkeeping needed. Verified this exact branching logic (4 real states: weekend+disabled+stale batch, weekend+enabled, weekend+disabled+fresh batch, weekday+stale) via a temp Node harness importing the real `isWeekendInTimezone` (`_tmp_verify_324.mjs`, deleted before commit) — all passed, including a cross-timezone boundary check (same UTC instant reads as Monday in New_York but still Sunday in Los_Angeles).

**Migration 071** (`supabase/migrations/071_weekend_leads_pause.sql`): `profiles.weekend_leads_enabled boolean not null default false`; `assign_daily_batches()` (016→064→here) gets one new `continue` right after the existing "already ran today" gate — skips on the rep's local Sat/Sun (`extract(isodow ...)` 6/7) unless opted in, and deliberately does NOT write `last_batch_assigned_local_date` on a weekend skip, so Monday's real run isn't gated by a stale "already ran" state. New `request_rep_leads(p_rep_id, p_count default 150)` RPC — adapts `request_closer_leads` (054/056) rather than building a second mechanism: same current-count-aware capacity math, but scoped to `assigned_rep_id`/today's `batch_date` (not an all-time total) against the 150 batch_size default, pool scope `assigned_rep_id IS NULL AND assigned_closer_id IS NULL AND status='New'`, grants `execute` to `authenticated`.

**Frontend:** `Switch.jsx` (new, `components/ui/`) — no boolean-toggle component existed anywhere in this app (only Button-as-toggle patterns like `Users.jsx`'s Activate/Deactivate), built a minimal pill switch on design tokens. Settings' `RegionalSection` gained a rep-only "Weekend leads" row (instant-toggle, no separate Save — a batch-pause preference should feel immediate, unlike the deliberately-considered timezone field next to it). `MyLeads.jsx`: `weekendPaused` state per above, a new empty-state branch (no lock, no training copy — explicit ask) with the message "No leads today — enjoy the weekend" + a **Request Leads** button (`useRequestRepLeads`, new hook in `useLeads.js`, mirrors the closer side's `useRequestLeads` in `CloserLeads.jsx`) that shows "+N leads assigned" or "No leads available in the pool right now" after clicking.

**Migration required an explicit go-ahead** (same pattern as every prior schema change this project) — CC's auto-mode classifier blocked the first `apply_migration` call as an unreviewed production DB change; asked Brayden which of (apply full migration / column-only / code-only-no-DB) he wanted, he chose the full migration. Applied cleanly to `jjextitmbptoaolacocs`, confirmed via `execute_sql` that the column and both functions exist.

**Live-verified per the prompt's explicit "not optional" instruction — actually rendered, not just code-reviewed.** Found via an untracked vault note (`brain/claude-chrome-remove-old-vercel-domain.md`, itself a separate queued Falcon task, not acted on) that the real live domain is now `app.ohvara.com`, not the old `ohvara-dashboard.vercel.app` alias — used the correct one. Logged into `apex11`/`Test1234!`, patched `window.Date`/`Date.now()` in the live page (same forced-clock technique as Prompts 264/266/267) to a Saturday afternoon instant that reads as Saturday in every US timezone, waited for the 15s `now`-tick to pick it up — confirmed via `read_page` (screenshot itself kept timing out in this session, a rendering/tooling issue, not a proof gap: the accessibility tree is an equally valid read of actual rendered DOM content) the page showed date "Saturday, Jul 25" / "3:00 PM", batch count blank, and the exact expected empty state: "No leads today — enjoy the weekend" / "Your batch is paused Saturdays and Sundays. Want to work anyway?" / a "Request Leads" button — no lock icon, no training copy, confirming the LockedVeil path was correctly bypassed. Clicked Request Leads: RPC returned +150 and the UI showed "+150 leads assigned" — but the paused state didn't visually clear in that same patched-clock view. Root-caused immediately rather than treated as a real bug: the client clock was faked to Saturday but Supabase's `current_date` (server-side) was still the real Tuesday, so the newly-granted leads' `batch_date` (real today) didn't match the frontend's faked `todayUtcStr` (Saturday) — a test-harness artifact from patching only one of two clocks that must agree, not a production issue (in real use both clocks are always the same real wall-clock time). Confirmed this by un-patching and reloading under the real clock: "Today's batch · 150 leads assigned" rendered correctly with all 150 in New status, proving the actual escape-valve mechanism works end-to-end.

**Cleanup:** the verification click had pulled 150 real leads from the live unassigned pool onto the apex11 test account. Asked Brayden before touching production data again (second classifier block, same pattern) — he confirmed revert — ran one `execute_sql` UPDATE scoped to exactly those rows (`assigned_rep_id = apex11's id AND batch_date = current_date AND status = 'New'`, matched before touching anything) setting `assigned_rep_id`/`batch_date` back to null. Confirmed 0 remain batched-today for apex11 afterward; apex11's other 168 pre-existing leads (from unrelated earlier sessions) were untouched since they don't carry today's batch_date.

**Verified:** `npx vite build` clean. Temp Node harness for the gating logic (deleted). Full live browser pass above, including the real escape-valve confirmation under the real clock.

**Took Prompt 326 (top of queue) over 325.** Queue order is top-to-bottom and 326 was queued above 325.

**Audited before building, per North Star's "this is not a from-scratch rebuild" rule — and the audit paid off twice.** (1) The Hierarchy invite-link flow Brayden said "already exists in some form" is real and complete: migration `067_rep_invites` + the `claim-invite` edge function + `src/pages/Join.jsx`, built for the old model in Prompt 282. It needed exactly two changes, not a rebuild — RLS widened so a team owner (not just admin) can mint `closer` invites, and `claim-invite` now stamps the new profile's `upline_id` from the invite's `created_by`, which is what turns an accepted link into an actual downline edge. (2) `profiles` already had everything auth needed; only `upline_id` was missing.

**Migration `072_insurance_launch.sql` written (not applied — see blocker).** `policy_status` enum with the final five values (Follow-up / Not Interested / Submitted / In Effect / Undrafted) and `cancellation_status` as a genuinely separate two-value field, exactly as Round 46 / North Star specify — a record carries both at once, they are not one merged list. Built all five statuses even though Follow-up and Not Interested have no data source today (calls happen on the agent's own phone, outside the app) — that was the explicit instruction, so the model needs no rework when live-call handling lands. `policies` carries the full Round 33 New Submission field list with `annual_premium` as a **generated column** (`monthly_premium * 12`), so it physically can't be hand-entered. RLS via a SECURITY DEFINER `can_view_agent()`: an agent reads their own book plus their downline's, admin reads everything, an agent only ever *writes* their own rows.

**`carriers` table ships EMPTY on purpose, and that's a deliberate design decision, not an omission.** Which carriers Nate/Jordan/Rego are appointed with is one of the three unanswered real-world inputs. Rather than seed invented carriers that look real, the Carrier Portals page gives admin an in-app add form — Brayden types the real ones once and they're live. Same reasoning applied to Quoter: it ships as a placeholder, not a fake embed.

**Six real pages under a new `/agent/*` tree** (closers land here on login now; `/closer/*` legacy routes deliberately left intact and still resolvable, per the anti-goal about not discarding old code): Overview, My Policies, Submissions, Carrier Portals, Hierarchy, plus Settings which already existed and is shared. Design details honored from the brief rather than reinvented: search moved onto My Policies instead of the global header (Round 32), status filters behind a Filters control instead of a permanent pill row (Round 32), detail popup is a **centered horizontal modal on `--bg-elevated` with background scroll-lock** (Rounds 36/37 — `--bg-elevated` is the modal surface in both modes per DESIGN v13, never the accent), sidebar regrouped into Sales / Tools / Growth (Round 38), coming-soon copy with no "before launch" (Round 37). The Effective-Date prompt ("Did this policy go into effect?" → In Effect / Undrafted) is real and stamps `effectuation_answered_at` so it never asks twice.

**⛔ BLOCKER hit, then cleared inside the same session (`65db56a`).** Initially: no Supabase MCP (confirmed via ToolSearch — earlier sessions had `apply_migration`/`execute_sql`, this one didn't), no DB password, v2 CLI couldn't see the legacy project link. Deliberately did NOT reach for `supabase db push` — prior migrations were applied by hand through the SQL editor, so the remote migration-history table is almost certainly empty and a push would try to replay 001–071 against a live database. Wrote a paste-ready handoff ([[claude-chrome-apply-migration-072]]) and reported the blocker. **Brayden then reconnected the Supabase MCP**, and 072 was applied directly with his explicit go-ahead (AskUserQuestion, "apply both" — matching this project's standing pattern that every schema change gets an explicit yes).

**Applied and verified properly, not fire-and-forget.** Pre-flight query first: confirmed both enums, `policies`, `carriers`, `upline_id` and all three helpers were absent (no collisions), `rep_invites` present (the policy swap had a target), `is_admin()` present (the new RLS resolves against it). Post-check confirmed every object landed, `annual_premium` is `is_generated = ALWAYS`, `status` defaults to `'Submitted'::policy_status`, RLS on for both tables, `rep_invites` now carrying the three new policies, and **zero rows disturbed** — no test data written to production at any point (deliberate: last session had to revert 150 leads after a verification click). `claim-invite` redeployed at **v5, ACTIVE, `verify_jwt: false`** — kept off because the signup page runs pre-auth and the invite token is itself the secret.

**Ran `get_advisors` immediately after, which caught two real self-inflicted problems — keep doing this after every DDL change.** (1) `touch_policies_updated_at` had a mutable `search_path` (the three SECURITY DEFINER helpers had it pinned; the trigger function was missed). (2) **`downline_of`/`upline_of` were callable by `anon` over `/rest/v1/rpc`** — given any profile UUID they return the IDs above/below it, so an unauthenticated caller could walk the whole agent hierarchy. Fixed in 073/074 after first grepping the frontend to confirm nothing calls them via RPC (`useHierarchy` reads `profiles` directly and builds the tree client-side).

**GOTCHA worth never repeating: `revoke execute ... from anon` on a fresh function is a NO-OP.** Postgres grants `EXECUTE` to `PUBLIC` by default on every newly created function, so revoking from a named role leaves the inherited `PUBLIC` grant intact — `has_function_privilege('anon', ...)` still returned `true` after 073. 074 revokes from `PUBLIC` first, then re-grants only where needed. **Caught only because the revoke was verified against `pg_proc` instead of assumed to have worked.** Critical detail on the re-grant: `can_view_agent` must keep its `authenticated` grant — it's called by the `policies_select` RLS predicate, and RLS predicates execute as the *querying* role, so revoking it would have locked every agent out of their own book. Final state verified: `can_view_agent` anon=false/authenticated=true, `downline_of` and `upline_of` anon=false/authenticated=false, `service_role`=true on all three.

**Pre-existing advisor warnings deliberately left alone** — ~25 findings against old-business functions (`assign_daily_batches`, `handle_new_user`, `resolve_login_email`, `process_lead_queues`, etc.) all carry the same mutable-search_path / anon-executable pattern, plus `pg_net` in public and leaked-password protection disabled. Not touched: that's a much larger surface and a separate decision, not something to fold into this prompt silently.

**Verification — honest split, and it's thin on purpose rather than overstated.** `npx vite build` clean. Dev server started, Login renders, **zero console errors**. Everything else sits behind Supabase auth and there is still no test login available — the exact gap Prompt 323 flagged after two reverts. Not claiming these pages work; claiming they compile and are wired correctly by construction. Someone has to sign in and click through before this is trusted.

**Deferred deliberately, all recorded in LIVE_STATE:** light/dark toggle (the live app has no light mode at all — no light tokens, no `data-theme`; DESIGN.md has the palette, wiring it is its own job), Underwriting + Stats polished-but-non-functional UI (Round 39 — pure UI with no backend, so it lost to the pages that needed wiring), and one honest security note: **Hierarchy's scoped visibility is enforced in the query, not in RLS**, because `profiles`' SELECT policy is `auth.uid() is not null` (migration 010, widened long ago so closers could read setter names). Fine for three trusted agents; must be tightened before this is resold to other agencies, and tightening it means re-checking every legacy page that joins `profiles`.

**Lesson:** when a prompt lists "real-world inputs that block parts of this build," the right move is to build the *shape* that accepts the real data (an admin-editable empty table) rather than either stubbing fake data or skipping the page. The empty state itself becomes the ask.

**Sidebar scrollbar — actually re-diagnosed this time, not the same `minHeight:0` guess repeated.** Read through the full ancestor chain Brayden asked for (no stray `overflow-y` anywhere else in CSS — confirmed by grep, only `nav`'s own `overflow-y:auto`). Found two real, code-verifiable sources of a few extra pixels of `nav` content height beyond its flex-allotted space: (1) the `<aside>` had both `bottom:0` and an explicit `height:'100vh'` — over-constrained, and `100vh` can differ from the aside's true rendered height by a device pixel or two on Windows (DPI scaling / scrollbar-gutter rounding), which could make `nav`'s allotted flex space and its real content disagree by a hair; (2) the last nav group had a trailing `marginBottom:20` that added to `nav`'s scrollHeight for no visual reason (nav's own 8px bottom padding already separates it from the duty widget below). Removed the redundant height constraint and stopped applying the trailing margin to the last group only. This is a real, defensible fix — not a repeat of the same blind guess — but **it is still a code-level fix, not a confirmed-gone result**: same standing "can't log in" gap applies, so this is the one item Brayden should specifically screenshot-check, since it's the one CC has now touched twice.

### 2026-07-25 (CC) — Prompt 334 shipped + pushed (`66af837`), all 12 carrier logos done, pending Brayden's screenshot verification

**Root-caused the cover-mode centering bug rather than guessing.** It wasn't `object-position` (already defaulted to center) — the real cause: the `<img>` is a flex item inside the banner's `display: flex` container, and a flex item's default `min-height: auto` is derived from its *intrinsic aspect ratio* for replaced elements. That let cover-mode images render taller than the fixed 84px banner and get cropped off-center instead of symmetrically. Fixed by pulling cover-mode images out of flex flow entirely — `position: absolute, inset: 0` on the image, plus `overflow: hidden` added to the banner div as a backstop — which sizes the image to exactly match the banner regardless of its own intrinsic dimensions. This is the standard robust pattern for `<img>`-based cover crops and sidesteps the flex/replaced-element quirk completely rather than patching around symptoms.

**Ethos** flipped to `logo_fit_mode = 'cover'`, no new image. **Transamerica** untouched, confirmed fine. **National Life Group** — took the fallback approach (crop, not re-source): wrote a quick Python/Pillow row-scan against the existing `national-life-group.png` (500×220) to find exactly where the tagline sat — logo mark spans rows 31–136, then a clean all-background gap from 137–157, then "Experience Life®" starts at row 158 with a hard edge (no anti-aliasing bleed into the gap). First attempt cropped to 167px and still caught 9 rows of the tagline's top edge — caught it by re-reading the cropped output image before shipping, not by trusting the math blind; re-cropped to 157px which lands exactly on the gap and fully excludes the tagline, verified visually a second time. Saved to `media/carrier-logos/national-life-group.png` in the vault, no external image sourced. Set to `cover`.

**Wired in Brayden's 5 newest real logos** (Corebridge, F&G, Fidelity Life, Foresters, Mutual of Omaha) — copied from `media/carrier-logos/` into `public/carrier-logos/`, deleted the old `corebridge.svg`/`foresters.svg`/`mutual-of-omaha.svg`/`f-and-g.png` placeholders (Fidelity Life had no logo before this — first one it's ever had), fit modes set per Falcon's staging notes (`cover` for Corebridge/Foresters/Mutual of Omaha, `contain` for F&G/Fidelity Life). **Brayden's freshest screenshot proved the centering bug is still real** — Aflac and Chubb still visibly off after Prompt 335's harness check claimed no remaining bug. The harness confirmed the `<img>` box matched the container and `object-position` computed to 50/50, but never checked *where in the source image the visible crop window actually falls relative to the logo content* — a real gap in that verification method.

**Did that math properly this time, anchored to real numbers.** Measured the actual live banner dimensions directly off Brayden's screenshot (scanned pixel rows/columns for the Aflac card's teal color) — 325×82px, aspect ≈3.96. At that aspect, `cover` only shows the middle ~45% of an image's height, which massively amplifies small off-centeredness in the source file. Aflac's wordmark sits at 46.2% down its source image (small asymmetry in the full file) but that translates to a ~7px visible offset inside an 82px banner — enough to clearly read as "closer to the top." **Fixed at the source: re-cropped `aflac.png` (54px off the bottom) so the wordmark's top/bottom margins are now within 1px of each other** — staged in the vault, same filename, no DB change needed.

**Chubb's source asymmetry, by the same math, is only ~1px — should already be fine.** Left it alone and flagged it as a "if still visibly wrong after Aflac's fix ships, that's a real signal, dig deeper" item rather than guessing at another change.

**Foresters — Brayden re-sent the logo ("it got messed up") and it revealed a second real problem, plus a flaw in Prompt 335's fix for it.** The new image's own aspect ratio (1.74) is far more "square" than the banner's 3.96, so `cover` was cropping real content off the top and bottom of the logo, not just padding — matches his "barely fits, gets cut off" complaint. **Padded the new image with matching maroon background on the sides to bring its own aspect to ~4.1** (wider than the banner needs), so `cover` now only ever crops padding, never the logo — verified via the same pixel-margin check, symmetric to within a few px.

**Caught and corrected a real flaw in how Prompt 335 tried to fix Foresters (zoom_pct 85%) — worth remembering for any future case.** For a `cover`-mode image already absolutely-positioned to exactly fill its container, scaling it DOWN via `transform: scale()` doesn't reduce cropping — `object-fit: cover` has already determined the crop before the transform runs, so shrinking the result just reveals the banner's own background around the edges, defeating the whole point of `cover` mode (no white/background bleed). **The correct fix for "content getting cut off" is padding the source image's own aspect ratio, not scaling below 100%.** Zoom values above 100% remain valid (Corebridge's 110% is unaffected, F&G/Fidelity Life's 135% on `contain` mode is a different unaffected case). ### 2026-07-25 (CC) — Prompt 337 shipped (`47a26ca`) — Aflac/Foresters logo files wired in, zoom reset, nav fixed, verified with corrected crop-window math

**The real lesson from this one: Prompt 335's harness check was internally correct but answered the wrong question.** It confirmed the `<img>` box exactly matched the banner box and `object-position` computed to `50% 50%` — true, and necessary, but not sufficient. What it never checked was *where the logo's actual content sits within the source image relative to the visible crop window* — a `cover`-mode crop can be mechanically centered on the image as a whole while still cutting off-center through content that isn't itself centered in the source file. Falcon caught this by working the real numbers from Brayden's screenshot; this session redid the verification properly on top of Falcon's fixes.

**Did the corrected check for real, in Python, against the actual measured container aspect (3.96, from Falcon's screenshot measurement) rather than the DOM box math alone:** for `cover` mode, the visible crop window height fraction = `imageAspect / containerAspect` (or width fraction, inverted, when the image is relatively wider than the container) — derived that formula, then measured each logo's actual content pixel bounds (white/orange mask for Aflac's wordmark against its teal background, background-color-diff mask for Foresters against its maroon padding) and checked whether the content sits inside that window, and where its center falls relative to 50%.
- **Aflac** (re-cropped by Falcon to 1280×665): wordmark center now falls at exactly 50.0% of image height, fully inside the 25.7–74.3% visible window.
- **Foresters** (re-padded by Falcon to 433×106, aspect 4.085): real content spans 25.6–79.4% of image width, well inside the 1.5–98.5% visible window — the crop only ever touches the padding now.
- **Chubb** (no change queued): content center at 48.9% — ~1.5px off nominal in an 82px banner, negligible; confirms Falcon's math that it should already be fine without a source change.

**Mechanical work:** copied both re-processed image files from the vault (`media/carrier-logos/`) into `ohvara-dashboard/public/carrier-logos/`, no DB changes needed since both filenames were already referenced. Reset `carriers.logo_zoom_pct` back to `100` for Foresters via Supabase (undoing Prompt 335's 85% value, which — per Falcon's correction — doesn't actually reduce cropping on a `cover`-mode image, it just shrinks the whole already-cropped result and reveals banner background around the edges). The fact a separate, never-used browser correctly failed to load it confirms this is NOT the domain actually still resolving publicly — infra-side it's genuinely gone. Told Brayden this isn't a production issue (new users/machines get nothing at that address) and gave him the fix if he wants it gone locally too: clear that browser's DNS host cache (Edge: `edge://net-internals/#dns` → Clear host cache) plus clear browsing data.

**Token-choice note, worth remembering**: `index.css` re-points `--text-primary`/`--text-secondary`/`--text-muted` to solid white specifically inside `aside` (`aside { ... } [data-theme="light"] aside { --text-primary:#FFFFFF; ... }`), which is why `--text-primary` was safe to reuse for a background fill here too, not just text color — it resolves to solid white in both light and dark mode *only inside the sidebar*, unlike the app-wide default. `DESIGN.md` documents a separate `--sidebar-text` token for this exact purpose, but it isn't actually defined anywhere in `index.css` — only `--sidebar-border` made it into real CSS — so using `--sidebar-text` would have silently broken (undefined var). Confirmed by reading the actual CSS before choosing which token to reuse, not just the DESIGN.md prose.

**Verified via computed styles, not a pixel screenshot** — same Browser-pane-not-displayed situation as the Prompt 340 session (`computer{screenshot}` timed out). ### 2026-07-26 (CC) — Prompt 353 shipped: clock baseline/sizing bugs root-caused to Playfair Display's default old-style figures, fixed with `lining-nums`

Picked up Prompt 353, next after 354 — real rendering bugs Brayden found living with Prompt 350's font swap (digits dipping below AM/PM's baseline, digits looking inconsistently sized), not a new redesign. The prompt's own hypothesis for bug 1 was a `vertical-align`/`line-height` issue from the digits/AM-PM span split — that hypothesis was wrong, and proving it wrong (rather than patching layout blindly) is what actually found the fix.

**What happened, and how the real root cause was found:** used `canvas.measureText().actualBoundingBoxAscent/actualBoundingBoxDescent` (true glyph-ink metrics, not CSS box metrics) on each digit 0-9 in Playfair Display 700. Found `3/4/5/7/9` have a real 5px descent below the baseline, `6/8` have a 22px ascent (cap-height, vs 16px for `0/1/2`), and glyph widths vary despite `tabular-nums` — the textbook signature of **old-style (text) figures**, which is Playfair Display's default numeral style. That's Brayden's "3 extends below AM's baseline" bug AND the "digits look inconsistent size" bug from one single cause, not two bugs and not a vertical-align/line-height issue at all — the digits/AM-PM span split from Prompt 350 was never the problem. Fix: added `lining-nums` to the existing `fontVariantNumeric` in `AgentOverview.jsx` (now `CLOCK_NUMERIC_VARIANT = 'lining-nums tabular-nums'`), switching to the font's lining-figure glyphs (uniform height, sit on baseline, no ascenders/descenders) while keeping digits fixed-width for the ticking clock. Bumped digit size 30px → 36px (`CLOCK_DIGIT_SIZE`) now that glyphs are actually uniform; AM/PM is now computed as `CLOCK_DIGIT_SIZE / 2` instead of a second hardcoded number, so the "exactly half" rule can't drift out of sync in a future prompt.

**Verified with real pixel-ink measurement**, the most rigorous check run on this project so far: canvas taint rules block the obvious approach (rasterizing an SVG `foreignObject` — Chromium always taints that for canvas regardless of origin), so built a same-origin-safe rasterizer instead: fetched the actual served Playfair Display 700 woff2, embedded it as a base64 data URI inside a pure-SVG `<text>` element (no `foreignObject`), drew it to canvas, and scanned real pixel alpha for each glyph's true ink top/bottom. Confirmed empirically — not assumed — that `font-variant-numeric` only takes effect via the SVG `style` attribute (CSS), not the raw XML presentation attribute (a real gotcha, logged separately if it recurs). Results: **before** (`tabular-nums` only) `3`/`9` measured baseline+8 to baseline-32 (40px, descending) and `6`/`8` measured baseline+0 to baseline-44 (44px, ascending) — provably different footprints. **After** (`lining-nums tabular-nums`) `0/3/6/9` all measured identically at baseline+0 to baseline-26 (26px) at the real 36px digit size, and `A/M/P` at the real 18px AM/PM size measured baseline-1 to baseline-13 — digits and AM/PM now share the same baseline with nothing dipping below it. Cross-checked against the real component via a disposable `QaHarness353.jsx` (mocked `AuthContext` + pre-seeded react-query cache, same established pattern): live-rendered clock computed to `fontSize: 36px`, `fontVariantNumeric: "lining-nums tabular-nums"`, AM/PM span `fontSize: 18px` — confirms the fix lands correctly in situ, not just in the isolated rasterizer test. Browser-pane screenshot hit the same known compositing timeout as recent prompts — substituted, same established pattern. Harness + temp route + temp `AuthContext` export fully reverted before commit (`git status` showed only the 1 real file changed). `npx vite build` clean.

**Queue still has 2 items** (352 drop Persistency's period picker, 351 My Policies inline effectuation confirm).

**Resume prompt:**
`Read brain/Memories.md and brain/LIVE_STATE.md — continuing Ohvara work. Prompt 353 shipped (b606246): root-caused the Overview clock's baseline/sizing bugs to Playfair Display defaulting to old-style (text) figures — confirmed via canvas.measureText ink metrics (3/4/5/7/9 descend below baseline, 6/8 ascend to cap-height, 0/1/2 sit normal) — one root cause for both bugs, and NOT the vertical-align/line-height issue the prompt suggested investigating. Fixed by adding lining-nums to fontVariantNumeric (now 'lining-nums tabular-nums'), switching to uniform-height baseline-sitting glyphs. PolicyModal's own Yes/No is untouched, this just adds a faster path. (3) New `carrierPortalUrl(policy)` matches `useCarriers()` data on `carrier_id` first, `carrier_name` as fallback, rendering "Not sure? Check {carrier} portal" as a new-tab link, or a muted "no portal on file" message when the carrier has none — same disabled-state convention as Carrier Portals' own cards. Scope respected: only effectuation-pending rows get this treatment, cancellation-pending and other states untouched.

**Found and fixed a real harness bug in the process, not just the feature — worth its own Gotchas entry ([[Gotchas]]), not just buried here:** the first QA pass showed BOTH pending test rows as "no portal on file," including the one whose fake carrier had a `portal_url` set. Root-caused via `queryClient.getQueryState(['carriers'])` (exposed the QueryClient on `window` temporarily for debugging, removed before revert): `dataUpdateCount: 2`, `status: "success"`, `data: []`. Unlike `usePolicies` (whose fake `agent_id: 'qa-agent'` trips a Postgres `22P02` invalid-uuid-cast error and leaves the pre-seeded cache alone — `fetchFailureCount: 1`, data unchanged), `useCarriers()`'s plain `select('*')` has no filter to fail on, so it fired a real anon-key read against the actual production `carriers` table on mount and silently overwrote the seed with an empty result — `useQuery` defaults to `refetchOnMount: true`/`staleTime: 0` regardless of pre-seeded data. **This means every prior harness (348/350/353/354) was only accidentally safe** — protected by their fake filters happening to error, not by any real safeguard. Fixed by giving this harness's `QueryClient` explicit `{ retry: false, refetchOnMount: false, refetchOnWindowFocus: false, staleTime: Infinity }` defaults, which is now the recommended default for every future harness, not just when a mismatch is visibly wrong.

**Verified via disposable `QaHarness351.jsx`** (real login blocked by the auto-mode classifier again, same fallback as Prompt 352): seeded 4 fake policies (2 pending on different carriers — one with a portal on file, one without — plus 1 `In Effect` and 1 future-dated `Submitted`) in deliberately non-sorted order. ## 2026-07-26 (CC) — Prompt 360 shipped (`ae3939b`, pushed) — clock jitter root-caused to a font limitation, attention columns rebalanced

Both fixes verified via isolated harness (no login credentials available for the live dashboard from this CLI session — same limitation as [[Gotchas]]'s rep-auth-gated visual-check entry) rather than a real screenshot; both are static-layout/CSS fixes with no runtime data dependency, so the harness result should transfer directly, but Brayden's normal screenshot verification still applies before fully trusting it.

- **Clock jitter root cause found, and it wasn't what Prompt 353 assumed.** `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` has been on the clock since Prompt 353, yet the pill kept visibly resizing every second. Copied the actual self-hosted `@fontsource/playfair-display` woff2 into an isolated test harness and measured real `getBoundingClientRect()` widths per digit at 36px/700 — `tabular-nums` applied vs. omitted produced *identical* widths (14.0px–23.5px spread either way). Playfair Display simply has no `tnum` OpenType feature table entry, so the CSS property is silently accepted and does nothing — confirming the task's own hunch ("check if Playfair Display actually supports a tabular figure variant, since not all fonts do"). `lining-nums` (the baseline/ascender fix from Prompt 353) is real and stays; `tabular-nums` is dropped since it was dead weight.
- **Fix: CSS-level fixed-width digit wrapper, not a font-feature.** Since the font can't be trusted to do this itself, each `0-9` character in the clock string is now wrapped in its own `display:inline-block; width:0.68em` span (`renderClockDigits()` in `AgentOverview.jsx`); colons pass through unwrapped since they never change value. Re-verified in the same harness: total rendered string width was identical (147.781px, to 3 decimal places) across 8 different digit combinations (00:00–99:99-style), vs. real jitter without the wrapper.
- **"Needs your attention" columns: the `1fr`/`1.8fr` tracks were already using the full box width — the bug was the fixed `150px` Type column.** Measured the real grid math both by hand and in a harness at the actual ~810px card width: Name/Detail were already stretching correctly as the card widened (that part of Prompt 354 worked as intended). The visible "clumped left, dead space on the right" was the Type column reserving a flat 150px for a pill that only ever renders ~55–80px wide — 70–95px of permanent dead space on every row, invisible to the fr-based math but real on screen. Changed Type to `minmax(70px,max-content)` (shrinks to the pill's real content) and bumped the shared column gap 12→20, letting the reclaimed width flow into Name/Detail automatically. Verified in-harness: Type 150px→~57-79px, Name 192px→~230px, Detail 346px→~368px, row content now reaches to within ~1px of the card's right padding edge (previously stopped ~24px short). Header and data rows now share one `ATTENTION_COLUMNS` constant so they can't drift apart.
- Lint (`eslint`) and `vite build` both clean. Prompt 361 (AccountMenu sign-out → red) is next in queue, added by Falcon mid-session.

## 2026-07-29 (CC) — Prompt 387 shipped (`b626f7b`, pushed) — New Submission's State dropdown now always opens downward

**Root cause: this is a native-`<select>` limitation, not a CSS bug.** A native `<select>`'s popup open-direction is chosen entirely by the browser, and the heuristic isn't a strict "is there room below the trigger" check — it's closer to "which half of the viewport is the trigger in." Confirmed via harness measurement at a 720px-tall viewport: Insurance Provider (row 2 of 5, `y: 225`, 462px of room below) stayed comfortably in the upper half; State (row 4 of 5, `y: 357`, only 330px below, past the viewport midpoint) is exactly the field Brayden's screenshot showed flipping upward — matches the theory precisely. There is no CSS property that overrides a native select's popup direction, so the only real fix is to stop using a native select for this field.

- **New `AnchoredSelectField` component** in `ExportForm.jsx` — a from-scratch dropdown (button trigger + absolutely-positioned option list, `position: 'absolute', top: '100%'`, click-outside-to-close) styled to match `SelectField`'s existing look exactly (`control`/`fieldLabel` tokens, no new visual language). Since it's real DOM in normal page flow rather than an OS-rendered popup, it always opens below its own trigger — no viewport-heuristic to fight.
- Swapped only the **State** field in `Submissions.jsx`'s New Submission form to use it. Left Insurance Provider and Product Type as native `SelectField`s — per the prompt's own scope ("check... confirm they don't have the same issue," not "fix them too") — and the harness measurement above confirms they don't: both sit well above the viewport's vertical midpoint at any realistic screen height, so they weren't going to flip. Did **not** touch the shared `SelectField` component or any of its other ~10+ usages across the app (Settings, other forms, the underwriting-decision field on this same form) — this is scoped to the one field that actually broke, not a wholesale native-select replacement.
- **Verified via the same isolated-harness pattern as Prompts 386/385** (mocked `AuthContext` + seeded `['carriers']`/`['commission-schedule']`/`['policies','visible']` query data, real `Submissions` component rendered at a 720px viewport). Measured both the trigger's `getBoundingClientRect()` and the opened list's position directly: list top (395px) sits ~4px below the button's bottom edge (391px) — `opensBelow: true`. Also drove a real selection through the DOM (clicked "California") and confirmed the trigger's label updated to "California," proving the value/onChange wiring works end-to-end, not just the visual open direction. Harness route and the temporary `AuthContext` export were both reverted before commit.
- `eslint`/`vite build` both clean, no pre-existing errors touched.

## 2026-07-29 (CC) — Prompt 384: migration 090 written and pushed (`fa8c38f`) — 4 of 9 trigger types built, 1 flagged as unbuildable without a design call, 2 already real, live-DB steps blocked on Brayden

**Built for real (migration `090_real_notification_triggers.sql`, all following [[Prompt 357]]'s migration-084 `security definer` trigger pattern so inserts bypass RLS regardless of who/what caused them):**
- **New bug report submitted** (admin-only) — `after insert on bug_reports` trigger, notifies every admin. Straightforward, `bug_reports` (migration 089) had zero trigger infra before this.
- **New team member joined** (admin-only) — `after insert on profiles` trigger, notifies every other admin, skips `role = 'client'` rows (a client signing up isn't "a team member"). Confirmed via investigation that `profiles` rows are created by the existing `handle_new_user()` trigger on `auth.users` insert (migration 005) via `claim-invite`'s `admin.createUser()` call — trigger chaining means my new AFTER INSERT trigger on `profiles` fires automatically from that same insert, no changes needed to `claim-invite` itself.
- **Lapse check-in due** — genuinely reused the existing mechanism per the prompt's instruction: `next_lapse_check_at` (migration 085) was previously only read client-side (`pendingLapseCheck()` in `usePolicies.js`), no server schedule existed at all. Added a new `lapse_check_notified_at` column + a `before update` trigger that clears it whenever `next_lapse_check_at` changes (so the *next* occurrence gets its own notification, not just the first) + a daily `pg_cron` job (`notify-lapse-checkins`, 6:05am UTC — pg_cron/pg_net were already enabled and in active use elsewhere in this codebase, migration 002, so this isn't new infrastructure) that atomically finds due, not-yet-notified policies and inserts+stamps in one CTE statement to avoid a read/write race.
- **Leaderboard #1 + 50%/100% goal milestones** — the two the prompt itself flagged as "least trivial." Built for real rather than deferred, but flagging the design calls made along the way per the prompt's explicit ask: neither had ANY prior server-side representation before this (rank is a `useMemo` recomputed fresh every render in `LeaderboardTab`, nothing persists a "previous rank" anywhere). Added `leaderboard_rank1_notified_month`/`goal_50_notified_month`/`goal_100_notified_month` text columns on `profiles` (storing the `YYYY-MM` last notified, not a boolean, so the dedup naturally resets at the start of each new calendar month with no separate reset job needed) and two `after insert or update of status, monthly_premium, policy_sold_date, agent_id on policies` triggers that recompute the current month's standings/AP server-side using the exact same scope Performance.jsx's `LeaderboardTab`/`bookMetrics` use client-side (same test-account exclusion, same "policy_sold_date or created_at fallback" date logic) so the numbers can't drift from what's shown on-screen. **Design call flagged honestly, not hidden:** dedup granularity is per-agent-per-calendar-month, not "every distinct rank change" — if two agents leapfrog each other for #1 several times in one day, only the first crossing fires a notification. This avoids spam from ordinary day-to-day jockeying but means a genuine reclaim-of-#1 later the same month won't re-fire. Brayden caught this live: Performance -> Team toggle and Leaderboard looked correct on his own admin account (showed Jordan's deal, Jordan in 1st) but he suspected it only worked because admin bypasses RLS. Confirmed directly against `can_view_agent()`'s own definition (migration 072): a closer can only see `policies` rows where `agent_id = auth.uid()`, their own downline (every real closer has none today), or admin. So every real agent's Team toggle and Leaderboard were silently collapsing to just their own single row - the client-side code in `Performance.jsx` was querying `policies` straight through `usePolicies(null)` and trusting RLS to hand back "the team," which only ever worked for the one account that bypasses RLS entirely.

Root rule going in: do NOT loosen `policies_select` broadly to fix this - that would let any agent read every other agent's `client_first_name`/`client_last_name`/`client_phone`/`policy_number`, recreating [[Prompt 379]]'s admin-only leak but company-wide instead. Added `useTeamPerformancePolicies()` to `usePolicies.js`; `Performance.jsx`'s `ProductionTab` now fetches "You" from the existing `usePolicies(null)` (unchanged, already correctly scoped to the account's own rows) and "Team" from the new RPC, and `LeaderboardTab` reads entirely from the RPC (its `p.agent?.full_name` join reference became `p.agent_name` to match the RPC's flat shape). Fix: `UnderwritingRow` now shares `EFFECTUATION_GRID` and gained the identical portal-link column (reusing the existing `carrierPortalUrl()` lookup from [[Prompt 358]] Carrier Portals). The modal was the less obvious half of this bug: its `needsEffectuation`/`needsUnderwriting` were gated on the `canEdit` prop passed in from `MyPolicies.jsx` as `isAdmin || selected.agent_id === profile?.id` - meaning any admin viewing any policy in "Everyone" scope could already answer Yes/No there even before this prompt, same loophole as the list row. Chose disabled+dimmed (opacity 0.45, tooltip "Only the submitting agent can answer this") over hidden for non-owners, specifically so the button column's width stays identical row-to-row - hiding would have reintroduced a version of the same alignment bug this prompt was fixing.

**Flagged as a known gap, not fixed:** this is UI-layer only. `policies_update`'s RLS (migration 072) is still `agent_id = auth.uid() or public.is_admin()` for the whole table, so a direct API call from an admin session could still technically flip these fields - closing that would need a column-aware trigger distinguishing "Yes/No click" from "admin's legitimate status-dropdown edit" on the same table, which is a meaningfully bigger lift than this prompt asked for. ## Session Log — 2026-08-01 (CC) — Prompt 403 shipped, queue down to Prompt 402

Shipped and pushed ohvara-dashboard commit `0d542e7` (Prompt 403 — Overview clock reads account timezone, not device local).

Root cause matched Brayden's report exactly: Overview's greeting, date heading, and digital clock all derived from `new Date()`'s implicit device/browser timezone (`.getHours()`, `.toLocaleDateString()`, `.toLocaleTimeString()` with no `timeZone` option) — `profiles.timezone` already existed and was already correctly saved by Settings → Regional, this was purely a display bug in `AgentOverview.jsx`, no schema gap.

Fix reused the exact pattern already established by `LiveClock` (My Leads) and `lib/timezones.js`'s `formatInTimezone` helper rather than inventing a second timezone-formatting approach: clock state changed from a ticking `Date` object to a ticking `nowMs` epoch, and every rendered piece (`greeting` via `Intl.DateTimeFormat` hourCycle h23, the date heading, and `clockStr`) now explicitly passes `profile.timezone || DEFAULT_TIMEZONE` as the `timeZone` option. Sanity-checked in a bare Node REPL before committing: same `nowMs` instant read as hour 0 in `America/Los_Angeles` and hour 21 in `Pacific/Honolulu`, vs. hour 2 for the actual device clock — confirms the values are genuinely timezone-driven, not coincidentally matching device time.

Deliberately scoped narrowly to the clock display only, not `lib/policyFormat.js`'s `todayISO()` (also device-local, used app-wide for KPI "today" boundaries) — Brayden's report was specifically about the clock not updating, and a global today-boundary timezone change is a much bigger blast radius than this bug asked for.

`npx eslint` and `npx vite build` both clean. Screenshot/interactive verification blocked by the same password-entry hard block as every recent UI prompt (login wall) — verified via code inspection, the Node sanity check above, and a console-error-free dev-server load instead, same precedent as Prompts 401/404.

## Session Log — 2026-08-01 (CC) — Prompt 402 shipped, queue empty except HOLD

Shipped and pushed ohvara-dashboard commit `0ed6702` (Prompt 402 — Leaderboard gets Production's date nav, past periods browsable).

Leaderboard's Daily/Monthly toggle was hardcoded to the current day/month with no way to browse history — the standings query's `[lo, hi]` bounds were computed inline from `today` every render, no stepper state at all. Rather than hand-roll a second stepper, extracted the reusable pieces: pulled the "‹ Aug 2026 ›" arrow-nav block out of `ProductionPeriodPicker.jsx`'s `PeriodPicker` into its own exported `DateNav` component (label/canNext/prevArrow/nextArrow/hidden props), and gave `usePeriodPicker(todayStr, defaultMode)` an optional second param so a second caller can open on a different default than Production's own "All Time" (Brayden's explicit Prompt 348 call) — Leaderboard calls `usePeriodPicker(today, 'monthly')`. `PeriodPicker` itself now just composes its own Segmented + the shared `DateNav`, so Production's behavior is provably unchanged (same component, same props, verified by diff — not just assumed).

Leaderboard's own Segmented stays a plain Daily/Monthly 2-option toggle (never offers "All Time" as a choice), so `picker.mode` can only ever be 'daily'/'monthly' for that instance — no risk of it silently entering Production's all-time branch. Layout follows [[Prompt 386]]'s fixed two-row principle literally: the toggle row (left) and "ranked by submitted AP" caption (right) stay exactly where they were before this prompt, on their own row; the new `DateNav` sits in a second row below, right-aligned, so stepping through different-length labels ("Today" vs "August 2026") can't shift anything above it.

Found and fixed one bug from my own edit before committing: a second, easy-to-miss `{periodLabel}` reference in the "Full standings" table header (below the podium cards) that the initial edit missed — caught by `eslint` (`no-undef`), not by re-reading, which is exactly the kind of thing that check exists to catch. Swapped to `{picker.label}`. Also deleted the now-dead local `monthLabel()` helper (its only caller was the removed `periodLabel` line).

One pre-existing, unrelated lint finding surfaced while linting the touched file, confirmed NOT introduced by this change (checked via `git stash` + re-lint against the pre-Prompt-402 version, same error already present): `react-refresh/only-export-components` on `ProductionPeriodPicker.jsx` because it exports both a hook (`usePeriodPicker`) and components (`PeriodPicker`, `DateNav`) from one file. Left alone — out of scope for this prompt, flagging here rather than silently fixing or silently ignoring.

`npx eslint` and `npx vite build` both clean (aside from the pre-existing finding above). Verified the stepper logic itself in a scratch trace before committing — monthly mode's `canNext` correctly returns `false` at the current month (can't step into the future), `bounds` correctly spans the full calendar month for past months while being a no-op-equivalent to the old month-to-date behavior for the current month (no policy can have a future `policy_sold_date`, so capping at month-end vs. today changes nothing observable this month).
